PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: ward-eve
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Wardrobe guard: transfer only textile rendering, light response, practical aging, and filmic material quality. Do not introduce white burial linen, blood, sandals, or a body identity unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
MUTED EARTH-TONE LINEN GARMENTS — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: COSTUME CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, FIT, DAMAGE, AND CONTINUITY.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Four-view cinematic wardrobe isolation sheet for Eve — First Woman Freed in JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL — focusing on her muted earth-tone linen garments as a locked production costume reference, not a full character performance portrait. Present the same complete costume construction across four panels: (1) frontal three-quarter worn-on-body view emphasizing drape, neckline, belt, and sleeve openings; (2) full-body front elevation showing length, hem break, and silhouette proportion; (3) side profile isolating side seams, underarm gusset, belt wrap, and vertical fall of fabric; (4) rear/costume construction view showing back neckline, rear drape, and how long white hair would rest over shoulders and upper back without inventing a second face. Use a matching ancient-woman silhouette only as a neutral mannequin-like wearer to hold the garments in true scale: elderly female proportions, slender aged frame, long white hair cascading down shoulders as continuity context for fabric-hair contact, one face only on the front of the head, no expressive performance pose beyond quiet standing with arms slightly away from the torso so sleeves and side seams read cleanly. Hands clean and anatomically correct, fingers relaxed, wrists free of jewelry.

Costume identity — muted earth-tone linen garments, simple ancient Near Eastern first-woman construction, distinct from Adam’s coarser rough-spun weave. Primary garment is a long ankle-length tunic-robe of handwoven linen, cut full enough for modest drape but thinned by millennia of captivity. Fabric is true linen: visible cross-hatch warp and weft, soft matte hand, subtle translucency where cloth is most worn over shoulders, elbows, and lower calves when backlit. Color is a continuous muted earth palette — dusty ochre, faded clay, pale sand, and ash-taupe — never pure white, never saturated dye, never modern pastel. Weave irregularities, slight hand-spun thickness variation, and age-softened edges sell authenticity. Secondary layer may include a simple open over-wrap or short shoulder mantle of the same family of earth linen, slightly coarser or a half-tone darker so layers separate under light; optional narrow waist binding of twisted linen cord or flat woven sash in matching earth tone, knotted simply at the side or front, frayed ends, no metal buckle, no ornament.

Construction and wear map (lock across all panels): round or soft V-shaped neckline worn thin at the collar edge; set-in or continuous sleeve openings ending mid-forearm or wrist with soft fray; side vents or gentle A-line fall allowing free step; hem reaching the ankles with uneven wear, small tears, and dust-darkened lower band from years of standing on hell’s stone floor; faint vertical crease memory from long suspension in chains; thin patches and translucent zones at pressure points; no embroidery, no jewelry, no beads, no crowns, no modern fasteners, no zippers, no buttons of any industrial kind. Continuity with imprisonment: light ash dust and fine soot settled in weave recesses; pale dried mineral dust at hem and lower skirt; subtle iron-oxide or blood-rust freckling only as environmental grime near lower edges if present, never fresh gore; fabric still recognizably linen, not shredded rags — dignified poverty of the first mother awaiting redemption.

Differentiate from related wardrobes: Eve’s linen is finer and more fluid than Adam’s rough-spun earth-tone cloth; still humble and stripped of possessions; no animal skins (those belong to Elijah and John); no royal blue/gold (David); no pure white divine robe (Jesus). No carried props in this sheet — Moses’ staff, David’s harp, chains, and sword of light are separate assets.

Lighting and material read for fabric: soft production key that reveals weave and wear without pure darkness — cool blue torch fill at roughly 2000K from one side casting gentle elongated shadows into linen folds, warm amber divine-adjacent rim or soft golden bounce at roughly 4500–6500K on the opposite edge to suggest the liberation beat when Eve reaches toward the Redeemer, subtle volumetric dust motes in air. Subsurface glow through thin linen patches; matte absorption in thicker folds; no glossy synthetic sheen; no plastic mannequin polish if a form is used. Color grade: muted earths and warm amber against cool blue shadows, biblical epic restraint, photoreal live-action, not illustration, not anime, not CGI fashion catalog gloss.

Camera and framing: multi-panel ingredients layout, each panel a clear production still; 2.39:1 cinematic sensibility within each view or balanced multi-view board; medium-to-full body coverage so neckline-to-hem is complete; depth of field deep enough to keep weave, fray, and belt knot sharp; consistent scale ruler implied by body proportions across panels; physically coherent anatomy and fabric physics. Sacred reverent tone of the first woman freed — costume of waiting and hope, not fashion spectacle. Hard constraints repeated: one face only on the front of the head; no modern objects, logos, readable text, captions, watermarks, borders, UI, or labels; no second rear face; lock the same linen color map, wear map, belt construction, and hem length in every panel so this sheet is the master wardrobe continuity reference for all Eve shots, including the moment of outstretched trembling hands saying “Our Redeemer...” and the later hand-in-hand ascent with Adam.
